package_info.package_manager: source (C++ library, used in OpenSAML/Shibboleth, included in proprietary Ivanti products)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a high-severity Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability (CVE-2023-36661) that allows attackers to supply malicious XML input, causing the library to resolve attacker-controlled URIs. This can be exploited to access internal resources, perform denial of service, or chain with other vulnerabilities for unauthenticated remote code execution in products embedding the library.

execution_context.file_location: Core xmltooling library (C++), invoked by SAML/XML parsing routines

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the application parses attacker-supplied XML, the code processes the KeyInfo element and resolves the URI in the RetrievalMethod, causing the server to make an HTTP request to an attacker-controlled domain, potentially accessing internal resources or exfiltrating data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing untrusted XML input to trigger arbitrary network requests is a classic SSRF pattern, enabling attackers to pivot into internal networks or exfiltrate sensitive data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal SAML/XML processing should not allow untrusted users to control URI resolution or trigger outbound network requests to arbitrary locations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate SAML implementations may fetch keys from trusted, pre-configured URIs, but not from user-supplied or unvalidated sources.
key_indicators: Unvalidated URI resolution from XML input
Network requests triggered by parsing attacker-controlled XML
No restriction on allowed URI schemes or destinations

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits malicious SAML/XML containing a KeyInfo element with a RetrievalMethod URI pointing to an attacker-controlled or internal resource.
attack_chain.leads_to: The vulnerable xmltooling library processes the XML and makes a server-side request to the specified URI.

attack_chain.action: The server-side request can access internal resources (SSRF), exfiltrate data, or be chained with other vulnerabilities (e.g., command injection) for further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential denial of service, data exfiltration, or unauthenticated remote code execution.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests during SAML/XML processing
Resolution of URIs from untrusted XML input
Access to internal network resources triggered by XML parsing
file_indicators: Application logs showing URI resolution during SAML authentication
network_indicators: Outbound requests to attacker-controlled domains from SAML gateway
Unexpected HTTP/HTTPS requests to internal IPs or sensitive endpoints during authentication
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor SAML/XML processing components for outbound network requests, especially those triggered by parsing user-supplied XML. Inspect logs for KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements with external or internal URIs. Use network monitoring to detect unexpected HTTP/HTTPS requests originating from authentication or SAML-processing services, and correlate with authentication events.
